slides.title: Where the time **actually** goes
paras: Re-reading CV #4 because you forgot what you liked about it.
Changing what matters halfway through the pile.
Writing "thanks, but no" emails one by one.
slides.note: The fix: decide what matters once, then check everyone against it.

cards.title: Scorecard builder
cards.text: I'm hiring a [ROLE] for my [TYPE OF BUSINESS]. Must-haves: [LIST]. Build a scorecard with 4 criteria tied to the job, each scored 0–2, with one line on what 0, 1 and 2 look like. No criteria about age, gender, names, photos, career gaps or where someone is from.

slides.note: Remove names, photos and contact details before pasting any application.

messages.text: Part-time barista, weekend shifts. Must-haves: weekends, serving customers.

1. Weekend availability
   2 = every Saturday and Sunday
2. Serving customers
   2 = 6+ months serving the public
3. Coffee or food prep
   2 = has used a commercial machine
4. Reliability
   2 = a role held 1+ year + a reference

slides.note: Example café, invented. It also defined 0 and 1 for each.

cards.title: Evidence check
cards.text: Score this application against the scorecard. For each criterion give the score and quote the line that supports it. If it's not mentioned, write "not mentioned" and score 0. Don't guess. Application: [PASTE, NAME REMOVED]

slides.note: No quote, no point. That's what keeps it fair.

messages.text: Available Saturdays. 2 years at a bakery counter. I make espresso at home every day. Happy to give my manager as a reference.

Weekends: 1. "Available Saturdays" (Sundays not mentioned)
Serving: 2. "2 years at a bakery counter"
Coffee: 1. "espresso at home"
Reliability: 2. "2 years" + reference offered
**Total 6/8.** Ask about Sundays.

slides.title: AI **sorts**. You decide.
paras: Never let it reject anyone on its own. Read every low score yourself before you say no.
Hiring rules differ by place, so check what you can and can't ask where you are.

steps.d: Aim for about a minute per application.
Plus any low score that feels off.
A kind "not this time" note, sent the same week.

caption:
How to screen job applications fairly with AI: a structured shortlist

The slow part of hiring isn't reading. It's re-reading, changing your mind halfway through the pile, and writing rejections one by one.

Prompt 1 builds the scorecard:
"I'm hiring a [ROLE] for my [TYPE OF BUSINESS]. Must-haves: [LIST]. Build a scorecard with 4 criteria tied to the job, each scored 0–2, with one line on what 0, 1 and 2 look like. No criteria about age, gender, names, photos, career gaps or where someone is from."

Prompt 2 scores each application with evidence:
"Score this application against the scorecard. For each criterion give the score and quote the line that supports it. If it's not mentioned, write 'not mentioned' and score 0. Don't guess. Application: [PASTE, NAME REMOVED]"

Remove names, photos and contact details first. AI sorts, you decide: read the low scores yourself before saying no, and check local hiring rules.
